evidence: Receiving DO2 drops from 11.45 mg/L (48.0h) to ~3.0 mg/L (49.2-51.6h), 2.78 mg/L at 52.0h, approaching 2.0 mg/L minimum
Receiving P assay at 48.0h (available 52.0h) = 3.00 g/L, matching source batches (2.98-3.06 g/L at 48h) — product on track
Source batches show DO2 recovery to ~12 mg/L by 28h after similar 24h dips, indicating feed-side modulation is effective in this process family
Allowed action reduce_feed = [0.8 feed, 1.0 air]: reduces oxygen demand while retaining product mass; no mass is discarded
args.rationale: Receiving DO2 collapsed from ~11.5 mg/L at 48h to 2.78 mg/L at 52h, leaving only ~0.8 mg/L above the 2.0 mg/L minimum, with a flat-to-declining trend. Product P at 48h (3.0 g/L) matches the source batches, so yield is not the problem — oxygen supply/demand imbalance is. A bounded feed reduction (0.8×) lowers oxygen uptake, restoring DO2 headroom without sacrificing product mass, mirroring the DO2 recovery pattern seen in all three source batches after their 24h dips. Aggressive interventions or a stop are unnecessary and would risk yield or produce zero counted production.
args.uncertainty: Hidden oxygen-transfer parameters and the true cause of the DO2 drop (uptake demand vs. transfer limitation) are unobservable. If it is a transfer/aeration failure, reduce_feed still raises DO2 but a combined action with air increase would be more robust; however DO2 near-saturation values earlier suggest transfer is intact and demand-driven depletion is more likely. Intervention response magnitude (how much DO2 recovers for 0.8× feed) is unquantified.
